subject: Post-call recap: Hyperscaler contrast — next qualification asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kiran Rao <kiran@dataforge.com>, Sara Lee <sara@dataforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Hyperscaler contrast — next qualification asks

Hi Kiran / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

What we heard from you
- Primary goal: reduce hallucination incidents in your customer-facing summarization flow while keeping average latency under 400ms for 1k token windows.
- Current baseline: you reported using Hyperscaler-A’s endpoint (v2) and Hyperscaler-B for burst capacity; rough hallucination estimate ~6–8% on your internal prompts.
- Constraints: PII cannot be logged; sandbox access needs to be on your VPC/whitelisted IPs.

What we propose for qualification (short & measurable)
1) Controlled probe: run a 2k-prompt suite (attached eval_prompt_set_v2.csv) across Redwood inference + Hyperscaler-A and Hyperscaler-B variants.
   - Metrics: hallucination_rate (closed-book fact checks), factual_precision (manual labeling subset), latency p50/p95, and token cost delta.
2) Regression checks: run previously failing prompts you flagged (IDs 21–32 in the CSV) and capture output diffs and KV-cache behavior.
3) Canary plan: roll Redwood as a secondary endpoint for a shadow run on 10% of production traffic for 48 hours (read-only) to validate distributional differences.

Immediate asks for DataForge
- Confirm which Hyperscaler-A model variant you used (exact model name + params) and sample request logs (redacted) for 10 representative transactions.
- Provide sandbox IPs or grant a scoped API key for the Redwood test tenant so we can run the suite.
- Prioritize the 12 customer prompts in the CSV that you labeled as "high risk".

Attachments: eval_prompt_set_v2.csv (prompt IDs, label guidance), hyperscaler-contrast-matrix.xlsx (empty template). Shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C-df-eval

Proposed timeline
- You confirm access + variants by EOD Wednesday (6/3)
- Redwood runs initial contrast battery by Friday (6/5)
- Quick sync Monday to review results and discuss a 48h shadow plan.

If that works I’ll schedule the short follow-up and loop in our infra engineer for whitelisting.

Thanks,
Marissa

--

From: Kiran Rao <kiran@dataforge.com>

Date: 2026-06-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Hyperscaler contrast — next qualification asks

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear plan. That all sounds good. Quick clarifications:
- Hyperscaler-A model is hyp-a/text-3.2-sft (we were testing default sampling). Hyperscaler-B used was hyp-b/gpt-lite-1.
- We can extract redacted sample logs; I’ll attach a redacted batch by EOD.
- Sandbox: we can either whitelist Redwood IPs (I’ll get that list) or provision a short-lived API key limited to the test tenant. Which do you prefer?

We’re most sensitive to hallucination reduction and latency staying below 400ms p95 — cost is secondary but visible. The list of high-risk prompts is accurate; prioritizing those is fine.

I’ll coordinate with our infra to push the access and send the logs. Please go ahead and schedule the first contrast run as soon as you have access.

—Kiran

Kiran — great, thanks. Whitelist is easiest for us (so we can keep the run reproducible), but scoped API key works if timing is tighter. Either option is fine.

A couple of additional specifics so our run produces directly comparable metrics:
- Hallucination definition: we’ll run a closed-book factual-check subset (200 prompts) and compute hallucination_rate = (# responses with at least one false assertion) / 200. We’ll also surface a "confidence mismatch" signal where the model asserts facts with high model-conf but low external evidence.
- Regression checks: we’ll diff token-level outputs and compute normalized edit distance for the flagged prompts (IDs 21–32); if edit distance > 0.35 vs your baseline we flag for manual triage.
- Cost: we’ll surface per-token cost delta assuming your current encoding (UTF-8, 1.02 tokens/word avg).

I’ve attached eval_prompt_set_v2.csv with labeling guidance and a small rubric for annotators. For transparency we’ll also attach raw outputs and a triage sheet after the run.

Proposed schedule update: if you can provide whitelisting or the scoped key by EOD 6/3 we’ll execute contrast runs on 6/4 and 6/5 and share a digest on 6/6.

If you want, Ben can join the first sync to talk pricing sensitivity and Dedicated options if we observe substantial cost delta.

Best,
Marissa
